questions.title: Top-down 与 bottom-up
questions.question: Compare top-down and bottom-up approaches to network design.
questions.cn: 比较两种设计方法。
questions.points: 先业务目标还是先技术；需求匹配、既有约束与反馈。
questions.answer:
A top-down approach starts with the organization’s goals and the needs of users and applications. The designer develops service requirements, traffic flows and architecture before selecting detailed technologies and equipment. This helps the network support the business.

A bottom-up approach begins with technologies, topologies or products. It can be convenient when a designer already knows particular equipment, but it may produce a network that fails to meet the real requirements.

For example, buying faster switches first will not solve every application problem. The actual problem may be delay on an external link or poor server performance. A top-down process investigates that need first. Existing equipment and technical limits still matter, so the process allows feedback. The key is to justify technology choices through requirements rather than personal preference.
questions.trap: top-down 不表示完全忽略现有设备。
questions.variants: Why is a business-driven design preferable?

questions.title: PPDIOO 生命周期
questions.question: Describe the six phases of PPDIOO and explain why network design is a life-cycle process.
questions.cn: 说明六阶段及持续循环。
questions.points: Prepare→Plan→Design→Implement→Operate→Optimize；优化反馈，不是装完结束。
questions.answer:
PPDIOO describes six phases: Prepare, Plan, Design, Implement, Operate and Optimize. Prepare establishes business goals and requirements. Plan gathers information, analyses needs and identifies an approach. Design develops the network topology and solution using requirements and knowledge of the existing network.

Implement puts the design into practice by installing and configuring the required solution. Operate manages and monitors the deployed network. Optimize uses operational evidence to improve the design or respond to problems and new requirements.

The phases form a life cycle rather than a process that ends after installation. For example, a new teaching application may expose a capacity problem during operation. Optimization may lead back to planning or design before further changes are implemented. This connects ongoing service quality with the organization’s changing goals and preserves the need for verification after deployment.
questions.trap: PPDIOO有两个O：Operate和Optimize；不要漏Prepare或把Plan/Design混同。
questions.variants: List the six phases; distinguish implementation, operation and optimization.

questions.title: Eight-step design methodology
questions.question: Describe the eight-step network design methodology and its documentation.
questions.cn: 说明八步方法与文档用途。
questions.points: 需求→现网→拓扑方案→实施计划→原型→完整文档→实施→验证监测修改。
questions.answer:
The eight steps are: identify customer requirements, describe the existing network, design the topology and solution, plan implementation, construct a prototype, fully document the design, implement it, and verify, monitor and modify it as needed.

Requirements include organizational and technical goals and constraints. The existing-network description records sites, devices, cabling, addressing, protocols and other relevant information. The solution should meet those needs, while the implementation plan explains procedures and timing. A prototype provides evidence before full deployment.

Documentation preserves decisions and supports future operation and improvement. The course suggests sections such as introduction, requirements, existing infrastructure, design, proof of concept, implementation plan and appendices. After implementation, measurements check the goals and guide changes. The method therefore connects planning and evidence with practical delivery rather than treating the final installation as sufficient proof of success.
questions.trap: 原型是验证方案的一环；不把课件文字中的prototype与全面安装混成一步。
questions.variants: List eight steps; explain the value of an audit, prototype and documentation.

questions.title: 分析、架构、设计的联系
questions.question: Explain how network analysis, architecture and design are connected.
questions.cn: 解释三阶段怎样相互连接。
questions.points: 需求证据 → 功能与关系 → 可实施选择；允许反馈，不是买完设备再找需求。
questions.answer:
Network analysis identifies what users, applications and devices need. It studies the current network, traffic, service levels and constraints. Its results give reasons for later decisions.

Network architecture uses these results to organize major functions, such as routing, performance, security and management. It describes their mechanisms and relationships. Network design then turns the architecture into practical choices of equipment, suppliers, services and physical locations.

For example, analysis may identify a need for reliable online teaching. Architecture may introduce redundant paths and traffic priorities. Design chooses suitable devices, links and their placement. The three activities depend on each other. If a design option is too expensive or cannot meet a requirement, earlier decisions must be reviewed. Keeping these links makes the final design easier to explain and defend.
questions.trap: 不要把 architecture 等同于设备型号清单。
questions.variants: Define each stage; why are they interdependent; explain defensibility.

questions.title: 网络要素与设备
questions.question: Describe the main elements of a computer network and their roles.
questions.cn: 说明终端、中间设备和介质的作用。
questions.points: host 起止；switch 局域网转发；router 跨网络；AP无线接入；介质传信号。
questions.answer:
A computer network connects end devices through communication media and intermediate devices. End devices, also called hosts, create or receive messages. Examples include computers, servers and printers.

Intermediate devices help messages reach their destinations. A switch usually forwards Ethernet frames within a local network. A router forwards IP packets between networks. An access point allows wireless devices to join a network. Other devices, such as repeaters and modems, have different connection or signal functions.

The media carry signals and may include copper cables, optical fibre or wireless links. Protocols and addresses make communication possible across these elements. A design must consider how the elements work together. For example, a fast backbone does not remove a slow wireless access link or a server bottleneck at the end of a path.
questions.trap: 不要把 switch 与 router 的典型作用写反。
questions.variants: Identify hosts, links, switches, routers and access points in a diagram.

questions.title: 网络类别
questions.question: Explain LAN, WAN, WLAN, CAN, MAN, SAN and VPN.
questions.cn: 解释常见网络类别，并区分分类维度。
questions.points: 地理范围、无线技术、存储用途、逻辑私网是不同维度。
questions.answer:
A LAN connects devices within a limited local area, such as an office. A WAN connects networks across larger distances. A MAN covers a metropolitan area, while a CAN links networks across a campus. A PAN serves a person’s nearby devices.

A WLAN is a wireless local area network. Wireless describes how devices connect, so it does not mean the network covers a larger area than a LAN. A SAN is a storage area network designed for communication with storage systems. A VPN creates a logical private connection over another network, often using encryption and controlled access.

These labels use different ways of classifying networks: geographical scope, connection technology, purpose and logical access. Therefore, one network can fit several labels. A university can have campus LANs, wireless access and VPN access through a WAN.
questions.trap: CAN 在这里是 Campus Area Network；不要混用地理范围与用途。
questions.variants: Choose a network category for a campus, storage system or remote worker.

questions.title: 网络组织模式
questions.question: Compare centralized, client-server, distributed, peer-to-peer, cloud-based and hybrid networks.
questions.cn: 比较六种组织模式。
questions.points: 角色、资源位置、管理及故障依赖。
questions.answer:
A centralized network places major control or processing at a central computer. A client-server network gives clients and servers different roles: clients request services and servers provide them. Central services can simplify management but may create important points of failure.

In a distributed network, resources and work are spread across computers. In a peer-to-peer network, peers can both request and provide resources. This can suit small sharing systems, although consistent control may be harder.

A cloud-based network uses resources hosted on remote cloud servers and depends on access to those services. A hybrid network combines models, such as central authentication with direct sharing between peers. The choice should follow application flows, management needs, reliability and cost. These models can overlap; a cloud service may also use a client-server model.
questions.trap: 不要声称 distributed 绝对没有中心；模式可以组合。
questions.variants: Compare client-server and peer-to-peer; discuss cloud dependence.

questions.title: 拓扑与故障
questions.question: Compare mesh, tree, bus, star and ring topologies.
questions.cn: 比较五种拓扑及成本、故障影响。
questions.points: 连接结构 → 备用路径与故障范围；物理/逻辑区分。
questions.answer:
A star connects devices to a central device. It is easy to extend, but failure of the central device may affect many users. Failure of one edge link usually affects only its attached device.

A mesh provides multiple connections and alternative paths. It can improve resilience, but it needs more links, ports and management. A tree organizes connections in a hierarchy. It supports growth, although a failure near the root can affect a large branch. A bus uses a shared backbone, so faults or contention on that shared medium can affect many devices. A ring connects devices in a loop; failure effects depend on whether protection or an alternative path exists.

Physical topology describes actual connections. Logical topology describes communication relationships. A suitable choice balances cost, scale, traffic and failure requirements.
questions.trap: 不能说任何 ring 断一条链路都必然全网停机。
questions.variants: Compare star and mesh; identify a single point of failure.

questions.title: Protocol 的规则
questions.question: What is a network protocol, and why must communicating devices follow common rules?
questions.cn: 什么是协议，为什么必须遵循共同规则？
questions.points: 格式、含义、顺序、时序、发送接收动作。
questions.answer:
A network protocol defines rules for exchanging messages between communicating entities. It specifies message formats, the meaning of fields, the order of exchanges and the actions taken when a message or event occurs.

Common rules are needed for encoding, message size, encapsulation, timing and delivery. For example, devices must know how to recognize a message, when to respond and what to do if a response does not arrive. Timing rules may include flow control, response timeouts and access to a shared medium.

Protocols can be implemented in software, hardware or both. Different protocols perform different tasks, such as application communication, routing and security. They must work together along a communication path. Without agreed rules, two devices might be physically connected but still be unable to understand or correctly process each other’s messages.
questions.trap: protocol 不只是设备之间的一根线或一种语言名称。
questions.variants: Explain encoding, encapsulation, timing and delivery rules.

questions.title: OSI、TCP/IP 与封装
questions.question: Describe the OSI and TCP/IP models and explain encapsulation.
questions.cn: 描述分层模型与封装过程。
questions.points: OSI 七层；TCP/IP 四层；发端加头、收端逐层解释移除。
questions.answer:
The OSI model has seven layers: application, presentation, session, transport, network, data link and physical. Each layer has a particular communication role and uses services from the layer below.

The TCP/IP model in this course has four layers: application, transport, Internet and network access. Its application layer covers several upper OSI functions. Its network access layer covers data-link and physical communication.

During encapsulation, application data passes down the stack. Transport and Internet protocols add information needed for process delivery and routing. The link layer places the packet in a frame, and the physical layer sends signals. At the receiver, corresponding layers interpret and remove the relevant information. Layering separates responsibilities and helps troubleshooting. It does not mean that each model layer always corresponds to one separate physical device.
questions.trap: 区分 packet、frame 和 signal；TCP/IP 本课用四层。
questions.variants: Name seven OSI layers; map them to TCP/IP; explain a web request.

questions.title: 应用协议、端口与 socket
questions.question: Explain the roles of application protocols, ports and sockets.
questions.cn: 解释应用层协议与进程定位。
questions.points: 应用协议规定业务消息；IP到host；port到应用端点；socket 接口。
questions.answer:
Application protocols define how applications exchange meaningful messages. HTTP supports web requests and responses, DNS translates names into network information, and SMTP supports sending email. FTP supports file transfer, while POP and IMAP support email access.

An IP address identifies a network interface for packet delivery. A transport port helps identify the application endpoint on a host. For example, HTTP commonly uses TCP port 80 and HTTPS commonly uses TCP port 443. A socket is an application’s communication endpoint.

Multiplexing collects data from different sockets for transmission. Demultiplexing delivers received data to the correct socket using transport information. This allows several applications to share the network at the same time. A web browser is an application; HTTP is a protocol that the browser and server use. They are related but are not the same thing.
questions.trap: DNS 不等于 DHCP；应用与应用层协议不同。
questions.variants: Distinguish a browser from HTTP; explain multiplexing and demultiplexing.

questions.title: TCP 与 UDP
questions.question: Compare TCP and UDP and explain when each may be useful.
questions.cn: 比较传输层两种协议。
questions.points: TCP可靠有序、连接、流控拥塞控；UDP无这些内建保证，应用取舍。
questions.answer:
TCP provides connection-oriented communication and a reliable, ordered byte stream. It uses sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmission to handle missing data. It also includes flow control and congestion control.

UDP sends datagrams without setting up a TCP-style connection. It does not itself guarantee delivery, ordering or retransmission. This makes its service simpler, but an application may need to provide its own protection against loss or congestion.

TCP is useful when complete and ordered delivery matters, such as transferring a file. UDP can suit applications that prefer timely delivery or use their own communication mechanisms. However, UDP is not automatically fast enough for every real-time application, and TCP does not guarantee low delay. The designer must consider application tolerance for loss, delay, overhead and the behaviour of the complete path.
questions.trap: 不要写 UDP 保证实时、TCP保证固定延迟。
questions.variants: Explain reliable vs unreliable service and connection-oriented vs connectionless.

questions.title: Forwarding、routing 与各层地址
questions.question: Distinguish forwarding from routing and explain link-layer and network-layer delivery.
questions.cn: 区分转发与路由，以及链路层和网络层。
questions.points: routing算路径/学习可达；forwarding查表送下一跳；MAC逐链路、IP跨网络。
questions.answer:
Routing learns network reachability and selects paths. Routing information is used to build forwarding information. Forwarding is the local action of moving an arriving packet to the correct outgoing interface or next hop.

At the network layer, IP addresses identify source and destination interfaces across networks. At the data-link layer, a frame carries data across a particular local link. Ethernet uses MAC addresses for this local delivery. The physical layer carries the bits as signals.

When a router forwards a packet onto another link, it usually creates a new link-layer frame for that next link. The final IP destination normally remains the same unless a mechanism such as NAT changes it. This distinction helps explain why routers need both network-layer forwarding information and suitable link-layer information for their next-hop communication.
questions.trap: 不要把 forwarding 的逐包动作与 routing 的路径计算互换。
questions.variants: Explain control plane and data plane; trace a packet through a router.

questions.title: Router 四部件
questions.question: Describe the four main components of a router and their roles.
questions.cn: 解释路由器内部四个主要组成。
questions.points: input ports接收；fabric内部搬运；output ports缓冲/发出；processor控制。
questions.answer:
A router has input ports, output ports, a switching fabric and a routing processor. Input ports receive traffic and perform the relevant physical- and link-layer functions. They also participate in forwarding operations.

The switching fabric connects input ports to the appropriate output ports inside the router. Output ports store packets when needed and transmit them onto outgoing links using the required link and physical functions. Queuing can occur when arriving traffic exceeds the available transmission service.

The routing processor performs control-plane work. In a traditional router, it runs routing protocols, maintains routing information and helps compute forwarding tables. In an SDN design, the device can receive forwarding information through communication with a controller. These roles explain the distinction between deciding forwarding behaviour and carrying out local packet forwarding. Processing, fabric and interface limits can each affect performance.
questions.trap: switching fabric是路由器内部连接结构，不是独立外置交换机的必然名称。
questions.variants: Relate router components to control/data planes and possible bottlenecks.

questions.title: Routing algorithm 三组分类
questions.question: Compare centralized/decentralized, static/dynamic and load-sensitive/load-insensitive routing algorithms.
questions.cn: 解释三种独立分类维度。
questions.points: 全局知识/邻居迭代；变化方式；cost是否反映当前拥塞；别把LS同物理单中心。
questions.answer:
The course classifies routing algorithms along three separate dimensions. A centralized algorithm uses complete network information to calculate paths. Link-state routing uses this global-information approach, even though calculations can be performed at individual routers. A decentralized algorithm develops routes through interactions between nodes; distance-vector routing is an example.

A static approach changes routes slowly or through manual intervention. A dynamic approach can respond to changes in topology or other routing information.

A load-sensitive algorithm changes link costs to reflect current congestion. A load-insensitive algorithm does not explicitly use current congestion as its link-cost input. These categories should not be treated as identical. For example, a dynamic protocol can react to a failed link without being load-sensitive. Explain which property is being compared before claiming that one algorithm is more responsive or suitable for a particular network.
questions.trap: centralized knowledge不表示一定只有一台中心机器；dynamic不等于load-sensitive。
questions.variants: Classify RIP/OSPF by knowledge and cost sensitivity; explain independent dimensions.

questions.title: Link、physical 与 service model
questions.question: Describe link-layer and physical-layer services and distinguish them from an end-to-end network service model.
questions.cn: 区分逐链路、物理传输与端到端服务承诺。
questions.points: frame相邻节点；bits介质信号；可靠性视协议；endtoend不由一个hop保证。
questions.answer:
The data-link layer transfers frames between adjacent nodes on a link. Its functions can include framing, access to the medium, error detection and correction, and, for some link protocols, reliable local delivery. A device uses a network interface to connect to a link.

The physical layer transmits bits through a medium, such as copper, optical fibre or wireless communication. Its operation depends on that medium and the associated signalling rules.

An end-to-end network service model describes the delivery characteristics offered between sender and receiver. Possible characteristics include delivery, bounded delay, ordering, minimum bandwidth or security. Best effort does not promise all these properties. A reliable local link is therefore different from guaranteed end-to-end delivery. Every relevant part of the path, and possibly the endpoints, must support the application’s actual service needs.
questions.trap: 不是所有link protocol都提供可靠交付；某一跳可靠不代表端到端保证。
questions.variants: Explain frames versus bits and why a reliable link is not a complete service guarantee.

questions.title: Strategic planning 与 Crouch
questions.question: Explain the purpose of a strategic network plan using the Crouch questions.
questions.cn: 用 Crouch 的问题说明战略规划。
questions.points: 使命/做事方式→现状→目标→路径→成功验证；gap、strategy/tactics。
questions.answer:
A strategic network plan connects long-term organizational goals with actions and resources. It asks why the organization exists, how it operates, where it is now, where it wants to be, how it will get there and how it will know that it has arrived.

These questions connect mission and values with the current situation, future direction and measures of success. Gap analysis identifies the difference between the present and desired states. Strategy sets the broad direction and deployment of resources. Tactics describe more specific actions used to carry out that direction.

For example, a university may aim to support teaching across several campuses. Its plan must connect that aim to network reach, service quality, budgets, staff and milestones. A plan is useful only if people can implement it, monitor progress and revise it when conditions change.
questions.trap: 不要把 strategy 写成某条具体设备配置命令。
questions.variants: Distinguish strategy and tactics; explain gap analysis and milestones.

questions.title: 规划建议与陷阱
questions.question: Describe good strategic planning practices and common pitfalls.
questions.cn: 说明有效规划方法及常见陷阱。
questions.points: 持续、简单、领导参与、创新、能实施、服务使命；资源/激励/照抄等失败。
questions.answer:
Strategic planning should be an ongoing way of thinking. The plan is never completely finished. Keep the process simple and manageable, involve leaders, encourage creative thinking and consider implementation before accepting a strategy. Planning should help the organization achieve its mission.

Common pitfalls include relying only on financial forecasts, collecting forms without real discussion and claiming to support planning without providing time or resources. Long-term plans can also fail when rewards encourage only short-term results. Other mistakes include copying competitors, blaming outsiders, weakening staff commitment and keeping outdated assumptions about the future.

For a network project, a technically attractive plan may still fail if no one can fund, operate or maintain it. A useful plan therefore links goals to resources, responsibilities and review. Success means improved organizational outcomes rather than simply producing a large planning document.
questions.trap: 六条建议、十条陷阱的完整清单见同题变式清单。
questions.variants: List the six tips or ten pitfalls; apply two pitfalls to a network upgrade.

questions.title: 四种变革策略
questions.question: Describe the four change strategies and the factors used to select them.
questions.cn: 解释四种变革策略与选择因素。
questions.points: Rational-Empirical利益；Normative-Re-educative规范；Power-Coercive权力；Environmental-Adaptive新环境。
questions.answer:
Rational-empirical change uses information and incentives, assuming people respond to their interests. Normative-re-educative change builds commitment by changing shared values and social norms. Power-coercive change uses authority and sanctions. Environmental-adaptive change creates a new environment and gradually moves people into it.

No single strategy fits every situation. Selection depends on resistance, the number of people affected, the stakes, the time available, the change team’s expertise and the dependency between staff and the organization. A large or high-stakes change may need a mixture.

For example, a network migration may combine explanations and training with clear deadlines and a gradual move to the new service. The course associates short time frames with greater use of authority, but this does not mean authority removes the need for communication or implementation support.
questions.trap: 四种是组织变革策略，不是四种 routing protocol。
questions.variants: Choose a strategy for strong resistance, limited time or mutual dependency.

questions.title: 规划团队与利益相关者
questions.question: Who should be involved in strategic planning, and why?
questions.cn: 谁应参与规划，为什么？
questions.points: 领导授权；实施者实践；使用者需求；信息/审核/记录角色。
questions.answer:
Strategic planning needs both authority and practical knowledge. Leaders, including the chief executive and board representatives, should guide strategic direction and support implementation. At least one participant should have authority to make strategic decisions.

The team should include people who develop and implement the plan, people who provide key information and people who review or authorize the result. Input should come from across the organization so that users and staff have a stake in the outcome. A coordinator should arrange meetings, record decisions and track preparation.

Team members should work well together, be committed and be respected by others. Membership can change as the work moves from mission and direction to analysis and detailed actions. For a network plan, this helps connect business goals with users’ needs and the realities of operating the network.
questions.trap: 让顾问独自决定并不能替代组织领导的参与。
questions.variants: Explain planning-team membership and changing roles across planning stages.

questions.title: Core、feature、future、rejected、informational
questions.question: Explain the five requirement categories used during analysis.
questions.cn: 解释需求分析中的五类归属。
questions.points: Core＝当前成功必需；feature＝希望有、可延后；future＝后续版本/升级；rejected＝已决定不纳入；informational＝背景信息。它们不同于user/application/device/network来源分类。
questions.answer:
Core requirements are necessary for the network to achieve its agreed purpose. Features are desirable capabilities that may be delivered later if they are not essential now. Future requirements describe needs planned for later revisions or upgrades.

Rejected requirements are considered unnecessary or undesirable for the agreed solution. The reason for rejection should be recorded. Informational items describe useful background, such as user numbers or existing conditions, without necessarily requiring a new capability.

These categories help control scope, resources and expectations. For example, access to a critical service may be core, an optional report may be a feature, and a planned new campus may create a future requirement. Classification should follow analysis and stakeholder agreement. It differs from classifying a requirement by its source, such as user, application, device or network. A useful specification can record both dimensions.
questions.trap: 不要把future当rejected；informational背景也可能用于推导真正需求。
questions.variants: 先遮住答案复述；再换一个场景说明分类、机制或条件。
questions.kind: 缺口补题；依据课件的AI参考答案

questions.title: MUST、SHOULD、MAY 与禁止性要求
questions.question: Explain MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY. How does the course relate these words to requirement categories?
questions.cn: 解释要求强度，并区别RFC词义与课件分类提示。
questions.points: MUST/SHALL/REQUIRED＝必须；MUST NOT/SHALL NOT＝禁止；SHOULD/RECOMMENDED＝建议、偏离须有充分理由；SHOULD NOT＝原则上不建议；MAY/OPTIONAL＝可选。
questions.answer:
MUST, SHALL and REQUIRED express a mandatory requirement. MUST NOT and SHALL NOT express an absolute prohibition. SHOULD and RECOMMENDED express a strong recommendation: an exception may be reasonable, but its consequences must be understood. SHOULD NOT and NOT RECOMMENDED similarly allow justified exceptions. MAY and OPTIONAL mean that a feature is genuinely optional.

The lecture links mandatory wording with core requirements, recommended wording with features or future needs, and optional wording with several possible project categories. This is guidance for analysing a project, rather than a rule that every optional item must be rejected.

For example, a system MUST protect an essential record, SHOULD provide a useful report and MAY offer an optional display. State the required behaviour clearly. A mandatory prohibition, such as preventing unauthorized access, is still a core requirement even though it describes something that must not happen.
questions.trap: 普通英文may不是自动在使用RFC关键词；MAY不等于rejected。RFC2119解释与课程管理分类要分清。
questions.variants: 先遮住答案复述；再换一个场景说明分类、机制或条件。
questions.kind: 缺口补题；依据课件的AI参考答案
questions.extra: RFC词义核对：[RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119.html)，§1–5。课件把这些词用于项目分类，不能把“MAY可选”说成RFC要求“必须拒绝”。

questions.title: 分类、Type、Status 与 Priority 的案例
questions.question: Classify a mandatory access-control requirement, an optional dashboard, a next-year campus expansion, an unsupported request and a user-count statement. Distinguish type, status and priority.
questions.cn: 给五项陈述分类，再解释规格表三个字段。
questions.points: 必需访问控制→core；可选dashboard→feature；明年校区→future；分析后决定不做→rejected；用户人数→informational。Type标来源，Status标当前处理状态，Priority标先后/重要性。
questions.answer:
A mandatory access-control capability is a core requirement. An optional dashboard can be a feature. A campus expansion planned for next year creates a future requirement. A request rejected after analysis belongs in the rejected category, with its reason recorded. A statement of current user numbers is informational, although it can support derived capacity requirements.

The specification also records other dimensions. Type identifies the source or entity involved, such as user, application, device or network. Status records the item’s current handling state, including information or an unresolved decision. Priority expresses its relative importance or order of attention.

These fields should not be confused. An application requirement may be core and high priority, while a network requirement may be optional and deferred. If an item is still unclear, record the uncertainty rather than silently treating it as approved or rejected.
questions.trap: Unsupported/unclear并不自动rejected，题目明确“分析后决定不做”才归rejected；TBD就是待确定。
questions.variants: 先遮住答案复述；再换一个场景说明分类、机制或条件。
questions.kind: 缺口补题；依据课件的AI参考答案

questions.title: 三种服务等级
questions.question: Compare best-effort, predictable and guaranteed network services.
questions.cn: 比较 best-effort、predictable、guaranteed。
questions.points: 无确定保证；可预测有受控表现；保证明确界限且需端到端机制。
questions.answer:
Best-effort service attempts to deliver traffic without promising a particular level of performance. It may be suitable for traffic that can tolerate variable delay or completion time.

Predictable service aims for a more controlled and consistent level of performance. Guaranteed service commits to specified requirements for an individual flow or service under stated conditions. Such requirements may involve capacity, delay or RMA. They need suitable resource allocation, control and verification along the complete path.

For example, a flexible download may accept best effort, while a critical interactive service may need stronger support. The choice must follow application needs rather than giving every flow the most expensive service. Services should be configurable, measurable and verifiable. A guarantee at one router alone cannot establish an end-to-end guarantee if another part of the path cannot support it.
questions.trap: guaranteed 不等于无条件永远不会出故障。
questions.variants: Why must a service be provisioned and measured end-to-end?

questions.title: 四类需求
questions.question: Describe user, application, device and network requirements.
questions.cn: 描述四类需求并说明联系。
questions.points: 主观用户需要转技术指标；应用端到端；设备限制；既有网络约束。
questions.answer:
User requirements describe what people need, such as timely responses, reliability, security, affordability and future growth. They are often less technical and need clarification.

Application requirements translate those needs into communication behaviour and service requirements, such as capacity, delay and reliability. Device requirements describe the capabilities and limits of end systems, servers and specialized equipment. Processor, memory, storage and interface performance can all affect the service. Network requirements include existing infrastructure, scalability, location, interoperability and support constraints.

These requirements build on each other. For example, users may want a smooth video lesson. The application needs suitable delay, loss and capacity, devices must process the media, and the network must support the complete path. Gathering only link speed would miss important parts of that requirement. Record user numbers, locations and expected growth as well.
questions.trap: host/device 是需求层级之一，不要漏掉终端瓶颈。
questions.variants: Turn a subjective user request into technical requirements.

questions.title: 应用分类与需求
questions.question: Distinguish mission-critical, rate-critical, real-time and interactive applications.
questions.cn: 区分应用类型及主导性能需求。
questions.points: mission→RMA；rate→capacity；real-time/interactive→delay；可兼多类。
questions.answer:
A mission-critical application is essential to the organization’s work. It needs suitable reliability, maintainability and availability because failure has serious consequences. A rate-critical application needs a particular data rate or capacity to operate properly.

Real-time and interactive applications have important timing requirements. Real-time traffic may become less useful if it arrives too late. Interactive users need responses within an acceptable time. These applications can also have capacity, loss and reliability requirements.

The categories can overlap. A live teaching service may be interactive, rate-sensitive and important to the university’s mission. Categorization helps identify where predictable, guaranteed or high-performance services may be needed. The designer should still define measurable requirements and application locations. Calling an application “critical” or “real-time” alone does not state the required availability, data rate or delay.
questions.trap: 不要把 mission-critical 直接等同于带宽最大。
questions.variants: Classify payroll, video, file transfer and interactive transactions.

questions.title: 需求分析五步
questions.question: Describe the requirements analysis process and its outputs.
questions.cn: 说明需求分析步骤与产物。
questions.points: 收集列出→指标→行为→发展需求→地图；spec持续更新。
questions.answer:
The process begins by gathering and listing requirements from users, management, the current network and initial project conditions. The designer then develops service metrics so that needs can be measured and checked.

Next, user and application behaviour is characterized. This includes user numbers, session frequency, duration, data sizes and traffic patterns. Requirements are then developed into more precise capacity, delay and RMA needs. Finally, the requirements are mapped to locations to show where services and performance are required.

The main output is a maintained requirements specification, supported by measurements and maps. The activities may be revisited when new information appears. For example, measured peak use may show that the original capacity estimate was too low. A clear process helps later architecture and design choices remain connected to evidence rather than assumptions.
questions.trap: 流程允许反复修订，不能把收集到的原话直接当最终可测试需求。
questions.variants: Explain a requirements map; describe inputs and outputs of each step.

questions.title: 初始条件、约束与红旗
questions.question: What initial conditions and warning signs should a designer examine when gathering requirements?
questions.cn: 收集需求时应检查哪些条件和警讯？
questions.points: 项目类型范围目标外力；预算/现网约束；real-time、百分比、high-performance需澄清。
questions.answer:
Initial conditions describe the starting point of the project. They include project type, scope, initial goals, the existing network and outside political, administrative or financial forces. Constraints may include budget, existing equipment, staff and organizational rules.

The designer should also look for unclear or unrealistic requirements. Warning signs include “real-time” without a timing limit, “high performance” without evidence, inconsistent requirements and availability stated only as a percentage without a measurement period or service definition.

These statements should be clarified through discussion and measurements. For example, “99.9% availability” needs a defined observation period, acceptable outage pattern and rules about maintenance. Existing measurements or a testbed can help validate the problem. Setting realistic expectations early reduces the risk of choosing an expensive solution that does not address what users actually need.
questions.trap: 说明99.9%不是错误；仅有百分比缺少口径。
questions.variants: Compare a greenfield project with an upgrade; clarify a red-flag requirement.

questions.title: 规格、测量与跟踪
questions.question: How should requirements be measured, recorded and kept up to date?
questions.cn: 如何测量、记录、维护需求？
questions.points: survey/访谈/测试；ID来源日期类型位置状态优先；变更可追踪。
questions.answer:
Requirements should be gathered through surveys, follow-up interviews, group meetings and observation. Measurements on the existing network help verify reported problems and current behaviour. A testbed can show how proposed technologies interact with the organization’s applications.

A requirements specification should record each requirement clearly. Useful fields include an identifier, date, type, description, source, location, status and priority. It should distinguish gathered statements from requirements derived through analysis.

Keep the specification current and accessible to the people involved. Record additions, changes and rejected proposals rather than silently replacing the history. This creates a useful audit trail. Measurements also need context, including time, load, method and units. A quiet-period measurement alone may not represent peak conditions. Good records make requirements easier to review, test and trace into later architecture and design decisions.
questions.trap: 不把瞬时测试或安静时段读数当所有时段的性能。
questions.variants: Explain gathered versus derived requirements and why change history matters.

questions.title: Capacity、throughput、delay 与 jitter
questions.question: Distinguish capacity, throughput, delay, jitter and task completion time.
questions.cn: 区分五项性能概念。
questions.points: capacity潜力、throughput实得、delay单次传送、jitter变化、TCT整任务。
questions.answer:
Capacity is the data-carrying capability of a network resource. Throughput is the rate of useful transfer actually achieved under particular conditions. A high-capacity link does not mean an application always receives that rate.

Delay is the time taken for data or a response to travel through the system. One-way delay and round-trip time describe different paths. Jitter is variation in delay. Task completion time is the time needed to finish an entire application task, such as transferring a file.

Data size divided by the allowed transfer time gives a basic average rate requirement after units are converted. Actual planning must also consider overhead, peaks, competing flows and end-system limits. Real-time applications may be sensitive to delay and jitter even when average throughput is adequate. Application duration should not be confused with packet delay.
questions.trap: 8bits=1byte；duration不等于delay；average不等于peak。
questions.variants: Compare peak, sustained and minimum data rate; calculate a rate requirement.

questions.title: 应用事务的频率与持续时间
questions.question: Why is it important to consider frequency and time duration for application transactions when characterizing application behavior?
questions.cn: 描述应用行为特征时，为什么考虑应用事务的发生频率和持续时间很重要？
questions.points:
频率描述应用事务多久发生一次，持续时间描述它保持活跃多久。两者帮助设计者估计流量何时发生，以及多少事务可能同时活跃。

例如，频繁发生、每次持续几分钟的事务可能重叠。共享链路和服务器于是必须支持多个活跃事务，影响容量、延迟和用户得到的服务质量。只看每天总流量可能掩盖繁忙时段。

因此，要把频率、持续时间与用户数、数据大小、流量速率和服务要求一起考虑。同样数据发送得更慢时，持续更久不一定意味着更高数据速率。理解这些因素有助于容量估计、flowspec和调度，例如把时间灵活的备份移出教学高峰。
questions.answer:
Frequency describes how often an application transaction occurs. Duration describes how long it remains active. Together, they help the designer estimate when traffic occurs and how many transactions may be active at the same time.

For example, frequent transactions that last several minutes may overlap. Shared links and servers must then support several active transactions. This can affect capacity, delay and the quality of service that users receive. A total daily traffic figure alone may hide these busy periods.

The designer should therefore consider transaction frequency and duration together with the number of users, data sizes, traffic rates and service requirements. Longer duration does not always mean a higher data rate, especially if the same amount of data is sent more slowly. Understanding these factors supports better capacity estimates, flow specifications and scheduling decisions, such as moving a flexible backup task away from a busy teaching period.
questions.trap: 只写“能提高性能”；把duration等同于delay；声称持续更久就必然需要更大带宽；完全不解释并发与峰值。
questions.variants: 如果两个应用每天总流量相同，为什么仍可能需要不同的网络安排？

questions.title: RMA 指标与边界
questions.question: Explain reliability, maintainability and availability and their relationship.
questions.cn: 解释 RMA 及其关系。
questions.points: R故障频率、M修复时间、A服务可用比例；统一故障/维修口径。
questions.answer:
Reliability describes how often failures occur. It can be represented by mean time between failures, or MTBF. For critical services, mean time between mission-critical failures, or MTBCF, may be more useful.

Maintainability describes how long restoration takes. MTTR includes the time needed to detect, isolate, repair and test a fault before full service returns. Availability relates the time between failures to restoration time. The course uses A = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR), or the corresponding MTBCF form.

Availability can improve by reducing failures or shortening restoration. Two systems may have the same availability but very different outage patterns. A frequent short interruption is not always equivalent to one long interruption for users. Define which failures count, the observation period and whether scheduled maintenance is included before comparing figures.
questions.trap: MTBF、MTTR单位必须一致；课件公式通常排除计划维护。
questions.variants: Calculate availability; explain why an availability percentage is insufficient.

questions.title: Availability
questions.question: A service has MTBF of 990 hours and MTTR of 10 hours. Find availability and two ways to improve it.
questions.cn: 计算可用性并提出两类改进。
questions.steps:
A=990/(990+10)=0.99=99%。两个时间均为小时。
减少故障提高MTBF；缩短检测、备件等待、修复测试降低MTTR。
若MTTR降至5，A=990/995≈99.4975%。这不是把可用性直接“提高5%”。
questions.answer: Availability is 990/(990+10) = 99%. It can be improved by increasing time between failures or reducing restoration time. The calculation requires consistent units and a clear definition of the failures and restoration periods being counted.
questions.trap: 不能用990/10；明确是否含计划维护。
questions.kind: AI计算变式；题值并非真实试题

questions.title: 可用性到停机预算
questions.question: If measured availability is 99.9% over a 30-day period, how much downtime is allowed?
questions.cn: 30天、99.9%的停机预算。
questions.steps:
观察窗口30×24=720小时；不可用比例1−0.999=0.001。
停机720×0.001=0.72小时=43.2分钟=43分12秒。
这个换算以该窗口所有计入时间为分母；若合同排除计划维护，应按合同另算。
同样总停机可以集中一次或分散多次，业务体验不同。
questions.answer: For a 30-day measurement window, 99.9% availability permits 0.1% downtime. That is 0.72 hours or 43.2 minutes. The result assumes that the full period is included in the measurement and uses the stated maintenance rules.
questions.trap: 99.9%并不自动说明单次中断最大允许时长。
questions.kind: AI计算变式；题值并非真实试题

questions.title: One-way delay 与 RTT 的计算和条件
questions.question: A forward path has 12 ms propagation, 8 ms transmission, 5 ms processing and 15 ms queuing delay. The complete return path takes 30 ms. Endpoint turnaround is 10 ms. Find forward one-way delay and RTT. Can an RTT limit of 100 ms alone guarantee at most 50 ms in each direction?
questions.cn: 使用互不重复的已给延迟项求单程和往返；检查“除二”假设。
questions.steps:
题中四项已规定为前向路径各项总量，不再按router数重复相乘。
前向one-way=12+8+5+15=40ms。
本题测量定义的RTT=前向40+终端turnaround10+回向30=80ms。
单独知道RTT≤100ms不能推出每向≤50ms。例如前向70、回向20、turnaround10仍RTT100。
仅在题中额外假定两向相等、端点处理可忽略，或明确分配预算时，才可用对称近似；它是额外假设，不是RTT定义。
questions.answer: The forward one-way delay is 40 ms. Including the stated return path and endpoint turnaround, RTT is 80 ms. An RTT limit of 100 ms alone does not guarantee a 50 ms bound in each direction. The paths may be asymmetric and endpoint processing may also contribute.
questions.trap: duration是事务持续时间；不是这里的数据包路径delay。RTT与单程的测量端点须定义清楚。
questions.kind: 缺口数值补题；AI自拟值或原表复算，见题内说明

questions.title: 数据速率、并发与单位
questions.question: A 60 MB file must transfer in 20 seconds. Estimate the payload rate and the total for five simultaneous transfers.
questions.cn: 数据量/时间与并发计算，MB采用十进制。
questions.steps:
本题规定1MB=10^6 bytes，1Mb/s=10^6 bits/s。
60×10^6×8/20=24×10^6bits/s=24Mb/s。
5个确实同时、均要同样进度且共享同方向瓶颈：5×24=120Mb/s payload。
另需协议overhead与合理余量；不能把100Mb/s链路当够。
若题中写MiB或规定1024制，要按该口径换算；不默默替换单位。
questions.answer: Each transfer needs an average payload rate of 24 Mb/s. Five simultaneous transfers need 120 Mb/s of aggregate payload capacity on the shared direction, before protocol overhead and planning margin. This assumes decimal MB and overlapping transfers.
questions.trap: 不要把60MB/20s=3MB/s误写成3Mb/s。
questions.kind: AI计算变式；题值并非真实试题

questions.title: 补充性能需求
questions.question: Explain operational suitability, supportability and confidence.
questions.cn: 解释三项补充性能需求。
questions.points: 能运行；能持续维护支持；按需要速率无错无丢可信交付（本课语境）。
questions.answer:
Operational suitability asks whether the customer can operate the planned network. It depends on both the design and the skills of the people who will use and run it.

Supportability asks what is needed to maintain effective operation after delivery. The course identifies RMA, workforce and training, procedures and documentation, tools, and spare or repair parts. A system that performs well on installation day may still be hard to support later.

Confidence, in this course, concerns the network’s ability to deliver data at the required rate without unacceptable error or loss. The acceptable level depends on the application. These requirements extend the design beyond nominal link speed. For example, a complex device may offer high performance but require training, maintenance procedures and spare parts that the organization cannot currently provide.
questions.trap: confidence 在此不是统计置信区间，也不是用户自信。
questions.variants: List the five supportability factors and give a design example.

questions.title: Flow 的定义与建立
questions.question: What is a traffic flow, and how is it developed from requirements?
questions.cn: 定义 flow 并说明建立步骤。
questions.points: 共同属性的端到端流量；源汇/方向/位置/服务；individual/composite/critical。
questions.answer:
A traffic flow is a set of network traffic with common attributes, such as source, destination, information type and direction. It is an end-to-end entity that can be associated with an application, device or user.

To develop flows, identify application requirements and locations, locate data sources and sinks, apply suitable flow models and combine performance requirements into flow specifications. A source produces data, while a sink receives it. The same device may perform both roles.

An individual flow represents a single application session. A composite flow combines flows sharing a link, path or network. A critical flow has particular importance or strict requirements. A flow map connects requirements to places in the network. This helps reveal shared paths, bottlenecks and where service mechanisms must be applied.
questions.trap: 不要把 flow 当成任意一条物理线；同一设备可同时 source/sink。
questions.variants: Explain individual, composite and critical flows; draw sources and sinks.

questions.title: 校园四类Flow：逐类图与合并图
questions.kind: Workshop原题；AI参考图，含显式假设
questions.question: Using Workshop Week7a Exercise 1, identify sources and sinks for all four flow types, draw each type, and combine them into one logical flow map. State assumptions where endpoints are not uniquely specified.
questions.cn: 按原图完成四类source/sink、各类型flow map与合并图；题目没唯一指定的端点要写假设。
questions.points: 先保留校园框与设备位置；再按四类流画逻辑箭头。External Access Server画在校园内。5台compute和2台storage分别分组。箭头表示应用流关系，不表示已知物理线缆。
questions.answer:
I keep the original device locations: compute servers in Buildings A, B and C; five compute servers and two storage servers in Main Engineering; and the external-access server inside the campus. Off-site archive storage and external users remain outside.

Type 1 connects participating computing devices. I use possible bidirectional communication between the compute groups; the workload must confirm the actual communicating pairs. Type 2 sends data from Main Engineering compute servers to its storage servers.

For Type 3, I assume the labelled external-access server is the intended migration destination and show participating compute groups sending to it. The wording alone does not uniquely identify every source or destination.

For Type 4, I assume Main Engineering storage supplies off-site archives. Internet access is shown separately, including campus communication with the Internet and external users accessing the campus server. The combined map preserves these flow types, directions and assumptions without inventing rates or physical links.
questions.trap: External Access Server不因external一词而移到校园框外；Type3目的、Type4归档源有歧义，图必须标假设，不能声称唯一官方答案。
questions.steps:
### 已给条件与记号

A、B、C为三栋楼的compute server；M为Main Engineering的5台compute；S为该楼2台storage；X为校园内External Access Server；O为校外Off-Site Data Archival storage；U为external users。

### 参考映射（AI补充；不是老师发布的唯一答案）

|流类型|Source → Sink|方向与已知/假设|
|---|---|---|
|1 高性能计算互通|参与计算的A/B/C/M组之间|参考图假设组间可能双向；M组内是否有互通按任务再确认；题目没给全配对清单，因此虚线表示候选关系，不声明所有同时活跃|
|2 主工程楼内部迁移|M → S|compute向storage，主方向由题干明确；不把协议ACK当等量反向业务|
|3 迁移到external server|参与迁移的A/B/C/M → X|参考图把X当所指server，是显式假设；若教师另指真正校外server，应换端点；X物理位置不变|
|4a 数据归档|S → O（跨Internet）|归档源假定S；若实际指定compute直接归档，按该需求改源|
|4b Internet access|校园参与终端 ↔ Internet；U ↔ X（跨Internet）|访问的请求/响应分别保留；X是应用服务器，不凭空把它当所有校园业务的网关|

### 画图步骤

1. 先临摹位置底图，保留Campus LAN边框，把X放框内、O/U放框外。
2. 单独画Type1，再画Type2。只有Type2的方向和楼内两组端点在题干非常明确。
3. 为Type3、Type4写上述假设，然后画各自图；未知流量速率、协议、具体路径保持未知。
4. 用颜色/类型标签把箭头合并。同一对端点可有不同业务流；不要因合并而删除方向或把不同服务保证平均掉。
5. 查是否保留5台compute/2台storage的区别、source/sink、外部用户访问与归档两类需求。要估容量还需每流速率、并发和调度数据，不能从图形距离推导。

交叉线没有节点圆点时，不表示交换设备或汇合；图只描述业务流，不确定实际物理拓扑。

questions.title: Workshop Flow 的方向与时延
questions.question: Label the directions and requirements of the four flows in Workshop Week7a Exercise 2.
questions.cn: 按原练习区分上下行、单向/双向与one-way/RTT。
questions.points: client-server双向1.2Mb/s下15kb/s上；video业务单向300kb/s40ms单程；Web双向250/100kb/s给5s；PoS双向30上50下100msRTT。
questions.answer:
The client-server application has bidirectional flows: 1.2 Mb/s from server to client and 15 kb/s from client to server. These directions should be labelled separately.

The UDP video application has a dominant unidirectional media flow from server to subscriber. Its requirements are 300 kb/s and 40 ms one-way delay. Any control traffic should be distinguished from the stated media flow.

The web application has 250 kb/s downstream and 100 kb/s upstream, with a stated five-second delay requirement. Do not silently reinterpret an unspecified delay as round-trip time. The point-of-sale application has 30 kb/s upstream, 50 kb/s downstream and a 100 ms round-trip requirement.

One-way delay and round-trip delay are different measures. Preserve the direction and measurement meaning in the flow map instead of replacing each application with one undirected capacity total.
questions.trap: Workshops周号不同于lecture；RTT不能直接当每一方向100ms。
questions.variants: 原题来源另见Moodle资料定位表 → Week7a Flow Analysis p.2 Ex2；Ex1四类flow及原图见Workshop原页与勘误。

questions.title: 四种 Flow model
questions.question: Describe peer-to-peer, client-server, hierarchical client-server and distributed-computing flow models.
questions.cn: 解释四种流量模型。
questions.points: 谁和谁通信，不等于物理拓扑；层级聚合、协作计算。
questions.answer:
A peer-to-peer flow model describes communication between peers that can both provide and request resources. A client-server model describes requests and responses between clients and service-providing servers.

In a hierarchical client-server model, servers can also act as clients of higher-level servers. Flows may be aggregated through several service levels. In distributed computing, multiple computing resources cooperate on a task and exchange data or intermediate results. This can create important flows between computing nodes as well as flows to storage.

The models help predict communication relationships and service locations. They do not directly specify the physical cable layout. For example, clients using a shared campus service may need a client-server model, while a compute cluster may also need a distributed-computing model. A real network can contain several models at the same time.
questions.trap: 模型可以并存；不是把四种分别当四种互斥物理拓扑。
questions.variants: Identify the model for email, tiered databases or a compute cluster.

questions.title: 选择应用与 Flow 优先级
questions.question: How should flows be selected for analysis and prioritized?
questions.cn: 如何选择分析对象并给流排序？
questions.points: top N需检查遗漏；业务/用户/安全/性能；排序依据变结果变。
questions.answer:
A designer may analyse individual applications, build profiles for similar flows or focus on the top applications driving the design. Selection can consider usage, user or device numbers and performance requirements. It is still necessary to check whether excluded applications will receive adequate service.

Flow priority should reflect organizational importance. Relevant factors include business objectives, consequences of failure, political priorities, performance and security requirements, and the number of users served. Different criteria can produce different rankings.

For example, a large student download flow may serve many people, while a smaller examination service may have stricter reliability requirements. The highest data rate is not automatically the highest priority. State the chosen criteria and explain how the ranking affects resource allocation. This makes later trade-offs transparent and connected to the organization’s goals.
questions.trap: Top N 不是忽略所有其他应用；带宽大不自动最重要。
questions.variants: Rank the same flows by user count and by reliability; explain the difference.

questions.title: Flowspec 与聚合规则
questions.question: Explain one-part, two-part and multipart flow specifications.
questions.cn: 解释三种 flowspec 及组合规则。
questions.points: BE合容量；predictable合容量取最严格delay/RMA；guaranteed逐流保留。
questions.answer:
A flow specification lists flows and their performance requirements. A one-part flowspec contains best-effort traffic and combines its capacity requirements. A two-part flowspec includes predictable traffic and may also include best effort.

For predictable traffic, capacity requirements are combined, while the most demanding relevant delay and RMA requirements must be preserved. In the course’s aggregation method, this means the minimum permitted delay and maximum required reliability or availability value. It does not mean adding availability percentages.

A multipart flowspec also includes guaranteed flows. Each guaranteed flow keeps its own requirements rather than losing them inside a single average. This is important because an acceptable aggregate may hide failure to meet one flow’s commitment. Aggregation must also respect shared paths, direction and timing. Opposite-direction or non-overlapping traffic should not be combined without stating the assumptions.
questions.trap: 不相加delay上限或availability百分比；guaranteed不被平均。
questions.variants: Compute a flowspec; explain why guarantees remain individual.

questions.title: Flowspec 数值组合
questions.question: Combine best-effort flows of 2 and 3 Mb/s, predictable flows of 4 and 6 Mb/s with delays 40 and 20 ms and availability targets 99.9% and 99.99%, plus a guaranteed flow of 5 Mb/s, 10 ms and 99.999%.
questions.cn: 按课件规则给multipart flowspec。
questions.steps:
BE capacity=2+3=5Mb/s。
Predictable capacity=4+6=10Mb/s；delay上限min(40,20)=20ms；availability目标max(99.9%,99.99%)=99.99%。
Guaranteed保留独立tuple：(5Mb/s,10ms,99.999%)。
若全在同方向、同链路同时发，初步payload需求5+10+5=20Mb/s。这个总和不抹掉独立保证，也不证明端到端availability已实现。
这里availability用作课件RMA聚合指标示例；各参数单位/测量口径须一致。
questions.answer: The multipart specification contains 5 Mb/s best effort, a predictable aggregate of 10 Mb/s with a 20 ms delay limit and 99.99% availability target, and the guaranteed flow kept separately at 5 Mb/s, 10 ms and 99.999%.
questions.trap: 目标聚合不是串联系统实际可用性的概率计算。
questions.kind: AI计算变式；题值并非真实试题

questions.title: 组件架构内部的相互作用
questions.question: Explain internal interactions of a component architecture.
questions.cn: 解释组件架构的内部相互作用。
questions.points:
组件架构包含功能、机制和内部关系。内部相互作用描述同一组件内的机制怎样彼此影响，包括取舍、依赖和限制。

取舍要求在相互竞争的收益间选择。例如，管理组件内集中式管理可能较易实施与管理，而分布式可以降低某些汇聚和故障风险，但增加复杂度。

依赖表示一个机制需要另一个机制才能达到目的。例如，性能组件内的SLA承诺依赖适当的QoS机制去落实服务要求；政策、SLA和设备能力必须相互适配。

限制是约束其他选择的条件。例如RIP等路由协议的能力限制了它能有效支持的网络结构。

答案应指出是哪一个组件并解释关系。不同组件之间的影响，如安全处理影响性能，属于外部关系。
questions.answer:
A component architecture contains functions, mechanisms and internal relationships. Internal interactions describe how mechanisms within the same component affect one another. They include trade-offs, dependencies and constraints.

A trade-off requires a choice between competing benefits. Within network management, centralized management can be simpler to implement and administer, while distributed management can reduce some concentration and failure risks but add complexity.

A dependency means that one mechanism needs another to achieve its purpose. Within the performance component, an SLA commitment depends on suitable QoS mechanisms being available to enforce the required service. Policies, SLAs and device capabilities must fit together.

A constraint is a restriction that limits other choices. For example, the limits of a routing protocol such as RIP restrict the network structures it can support effectively.

The answer should identify the component and explain the relationship. Effects between separate components, such as security processing affecting performance, are external relationships.
questions.trap: 只列四个component名称；只写“互相影响”而无关系与例子；把external写成internal。
questions.variants: QoS执行SLA与加密增加延迟，哪一个更直接是本题的内部关系例子？为什么？

questions.title: 内部关系与外部关系
questions.question: Distinguish internal and external relationships in network architecture.
questions.cn: 区分组件内部与组件之间的关系。
questions.points: 同一功能内部 vs 不同功能之间；trade-off/dependency/constraint。
questions.answer:
Internal relationships exist between mechanisms within one component architecture. They include trade-offs, dependencies and constraints. For example, within performance architecture, a policy may depend on QoS mechanisms to enforce a service level agreement.

External relationships exist between different component architectures. For example, security inspection can affect performance, management traffic depends on addressing and routing, and management access can create security exposure.

The classification depends on the functions being compared, not simply whether the devices are in the same building. A reference architecture combines the component architectures and their relationships. It must balance them according to requirements and flow priorities. Optimizing each component alone may give a poor overall result. For instance, extensive inspection may improve one security goal while making a critical application miss its delay requirement.
questions.trap: internal/external 不等于机构内网/公网。
questions.variants: Classify a QoS–SLA relationship and a security–performance relationship.

questions.title: Reference architecture 的形成
questions.question: How are component architectures and architectural models combined into a reference architecture?
questions.cn: 如何把组件架构和模型合成参考架构？
questions.points: 完整功能/内部外部关系；topological打底，再叠加flow/functional。
questions.answer:
A reference architecture describes the complete network architecture. It combines the selected component architectures, their mechanisms and the internal and external relationships that affect the whole system.

The course suggests starting with a topological model, such as LAN/MAN/WAN or access/distribution/core. Flow-based models then describe important communication relationships. Functional models add perspectives such as service delivery, intranet/extranet separation or complete end-to-end paths.

These models are complementary views. For example, a campus can use an access/distribution/core structure, support client-server flows and provide controlled extranet access for partners. The designer then checks how routing, management, performance and security work together within that structure. Requirements and flow priorities determine the balance. A reference architecture is therefore more than a topology drawing or a collection of separate product choices.
questions.trap: 回答所有模型时请用Q06的完整清单；不要漏functional三类。
questions.variants: Explain the recipe for using architectural models; give a combined example.

questions.title: 课堂讨论的全部架构模型
questions.question: Briefly describe all architectural model as discussed in the lectures.
questions.cn: 简要描述课堂讨论过的所有架构模型。
questions.points:
课堂讨论三组架构模型。拓扑类包含LAN/MAN/WAN，即按地理尺度组织网络，以及access/distribution/core，即按功能层次组织网络。

流量类描述通信模式。对等模式使通信实体处于相近层级；客户端—服务器模式关注双方通信；分层客户端—服务器加入服务器层级及层间通信；分布式计算描述协作计算资源及其数据交换。

功能类围绕服务或访问要求组织架构。服务提供方模型关注服务交付、隐私和安全等提供方功能；内网/外网模型根据内部使用和被许可的外部使用划分访问；端到端模型考虑完整流量路径上的所有组件。

这些视角可以组合。设计者可从拓扑模型开始，添加流量与功能视角，形成满足需求的参考架构。这些是互补视角，不是单一通用解法。
questions.answer:
The lectures discuss three groups of architectural models. Topological models include LAN/MAN/WAN, which organizes the network by geographical scale, and access/distribution/core, which organizes it by functional layers.

Flow-based models describe communication patterns. Peer-to-peer places communicating entities at a similar level. Client-server focuses on communication between clients and servers. Hierarchical client-server adds server tiers and communication between them. Distributed computing describes cooperating computing resources and their data exchanges.

Functional models organize the architecture around services or access requirements. The service-provider model focuses on provider functions such as service delivery, privacy and security. The intranet/extranet model separates access according to internal and permitted external use. The end-to-end model considers all components along a complete traffic path.

These views can be combined. A designer can start with a topological model and add flow-based and functional views to form a reference architecture that meets the requirements. They are complementary views rather than a single universal solution.
questions.trap: 只写三类名称；漏functional三项；将模型误答为OSI、TCP/IP、SDN；只列清单不描述。
questions.variants: “按建筑之间的地理尺度”和“按一条业务的完整路径”分别属于哪种模型？

questions.title: CIA 与 privacy
questions.question: Explain confidentiality, integrity, availability and privacy in strategic network design.
questions.cn: 解释安全目标与隐私。
questions.points: C防泄露、I防未授权修改、A合法用户可用；privacy含个人信息恰当使用。
questions.answer:
Confidentiality means that information is available only to authorized parties. Integrity means that information and resources are protected against unauthorized change or corruption. Availability means that authorized users can obtain required services when needed.

Privacy concerns the appropriate collection, use, access and disclosure of personal information. It overlaps with security, but protecting data from attackers does not by itself make every use of that data appropriate.

These goals matter because organizations depend on networks for work and communication. Loss of confidentiality may expose records, loss of integrity may make decisions unreliable, and loss of availability may stop services. The design should identify important assets and threats, select suitable controls and consider operational trade-offs. Security and privacy should shape architecture from the beginning rather than being added only as a final device.
questions.trap: 加密主要保密，不能单独保证CIA全目标。
questions.variants: Explain why security and privacy are strategic rather than optional add-ons.

questions.title: Threat analysis 与风险排序
questions.question: Why is threat analysis important, and what should it consider?
questions.cn: 为什么做威胁分析，应考虑什么？
questions.points: asset→threat→likelihood+impact→优先级→措施→复查；多方减少主观性。
questions.answer:
Threat analysis identifies assets that need protection and the threats that may harm them. Assets include devices, software, services and data. Threats include unauthorized access or disclosure, denial of service, theft, corruption, malware and physical damage.

For each important asset–threat combination, assess the likelihood and the potential cost or damage. The impact depends on organizational goals. A threat with both high likelihood and serious consequences needs a plan to reduce the risk to an acceptable level.

The results guide priorities, control selection and resource allocation. For example, protecting a critical teaching service may require stronger availability controls than protecting a low-priority test service. Analysis is partly subjective, so involve different groups and record assumptions. Review it periodically because assets, services, users and threats change. A list of threats without consequences or priorities is incomplete.
questions.trap: 风险不只看攻击概率，还要看业务损害。
questions.variants: Name three threats and connect each to an asset, impact and control.

questions.title: 填写 Threat analysis worksheet
questions.question: Complete a threat-analysis worksheet for student records, online teaching and stored research data. Explain how the results guide priorities.
questions.cn: 对三个资产给出威胁、可能性、损害和措施。
questions.points:
worksheet不是只列攻击名。示例：学生记录—未授权访问—泄露/修改；教学—DoS—停课；研究存储—恶意软件/损坏—数据丢失。概率和损失无原始数据时标待评估，不编造百分比。

|资产|威胁|可能性|业务损害|可选控制|后续证据|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|学生记录|未授权访问/披露|待评估，不捏造百分比|隐私泄露、记录完整性受损|认证、最小访问、审计|用户/管理员访谈、访问记录|
|在线教学服务|DoS|待评估|课堂中断、服务不可用|适当流量控制、冗余与恢复计划|服务日志、依赖和容量测试|
|研究存储|恶意软件/数据损坏|待评估|研究数据不可用或错误|访问控制、保护、经测试恢复|备份恢复证据、系统维护记录|

这是课堂框架上的AI示例；控制是否充分、风险排序需结合实际概率和损失，不能只凭资产名称下结论。
questions.answer:
A threat-analysis worksheet connects each asset with a threat, its likelihood, possible damage and an appropriate response. For student records, unauthorized access could expose personal data or change results. Access control, authentication and logging can reduce that risk.

For online teaching, denial of service can interrupt classes. Appropriate traffic controls and resilience planning can reduce the impact. For research storage, malware or data corruption can destroy useful work. Protection, controlled access and tested recovery procedures can support restoration.

These are illustrative scenarios, not measured probabilities for a real university. Record likelihood as needing assessment unless evidence is available. Estimate impact in relation to the organization’s goals and involve the relevant users and staff. High-likelihood, high-impact combinations require particular attention. The worksheet should guide priorities and controls and be reviewed when assets, threats or services change.
questions.trap: 没有数据就不要凭空写“80%攻击概率”；控制措施不能写成已保证零风险。
questions.variants: 先遮住答案复述；再换一个场景说明分类、机制或条件。
questions.kind: 缺口补题；依据课件的AI参考答案

questions.title: Security policies 与 procedures
questions.question: What should security policies and procedures contain?
questions.cn: 安全政策与流程应包含什么？
questions.points: 规则和理由；隐私/责任/认证/报告；配置补丁备份/应急；服务组织目标。
questions.answer:
Security policies state rules for access and acceptable use. Procedures describe how people carry out those rules. They should explain both what to do and why it reduces risk.

The course includes privacy statements about monitoring, logging and access; accountability and auditing responsibilities; authentication rules, including passwords and remote access; and ways to report violations. Other areas include administrator skills, device connection, configuration changes, patching, malware protection, backups, offsite storage and contingency plans.

For example, an access policy may limit who can view student records. A procedure explains how access is approved, reviewed and removed. Rules should be practical and support organizational goals. Excessive control can prevent useful work without producing a proportionate security benefit. Policies also need responsible owners, user awareness and regular review as the network changes.
questions.trap: policy是规则，procedure是执行步骤；不能只堆设备名。
questions.variants: Describe privacy, accountability, authentication and incident-reporting statements.

questions.title: 默认允许与默认拒绝的安全哲学
questions.question: Compare the two security philosophies shown in the lecture: deny specifics/accept everything else and accept specifics/deny everything else.
questions.cn: 按原图比较默认放行与默认拒绝。
questions.points: 左图deny list：明确拒绝命中项，其余通过；右图allow list：明确允许命中项，其余丢弃。开放性/控制范围/维护要求取舍；不是“四种哲学”。
questions.answer:
The first philosophy denies specified traffic and accepts everything else. It is an open approach: traffic matching the deny rules is dropped, while other traffic passes. This can make new communication easier, but an unlisted unwanted flow may also pass.

The second philosophy accepts specified traffic and denies everything else. It is a closed approach: traffic matching the permit rules passes, while other traffic is dropped. This limits access to known allowed communication but requires careful identification and maintenance of legitimate flows.

The choice affects both risk and useful work. For a sensitive service, explicitly defining permitted communication may support its protection goals. However, incomplete rules can block required access or management. A designer should connect the philosophy to threats, required flows and organizational needs, test the rules, and explain how changes will be handled.
questions.trap: 这是图中的策略逻辑，不能等同某设备ACL语法已配置好；默认拒绝也需正确允许合法业务。
questions.variants: 先遮住答案复述；再换一个场景说明分类、机制或条件。
questions.kind: 缺口补题；依据课件的AI参考答案

questions.title: 物理安全与 packet filtering
questions.question: Describe physical security and packet filtering, including their limits.
questions.cn: 描述物理安全和包过滤，并说明局限。
questions.points: 机房/设备接触控制；IP/port allow/deny；单项控制不覆盖所有威胁。
questions.answer:
Physical security protects equipment and facilities from unauthorized access, theft or damage. Measures can include controlled rooms, locked cabinets and appropriate environmental protection. These measures matter because physical access can bypass some logical controls or interrupt service.

Packet filtering permits or denies traffic according to defined rules, such as source or destination IP addresses, protocols and port numbers. It can restrict access to a server or separate network zones.

These mechanisms address different risks and work best together. A locked server room does not stop an attacker using an allowed network service. A packet filter does not prove that every permitted message is safe or that its sender is trustworthy. Filters require correct rules, maintenance and testing. Their placement should follow asset locations, communication requirements and the organization’s security policy.
questions.trap: 允许端口不代表该端口所有内容都安全。
questions.variants: Give one physical control and one logical control for a server.

questions.title: IPsec、SNMPv3 与 encryption
questions.question: Explain IPsec, SNMPv3 and encryption as security mechanisms.
questions.cn: 解释三种协议/机制怎样保护通信。
questions.points: IPsec网络层传输/隧道；SNMPv3保护管理消息；加密及密钥管理。
questions.answer:
IPsec provides security functions at the IP layer. Depending on the selected mechanisms, it can support authentication, integrity and encryption. Transport mode protects communication between endpoints, while tunnel mode carries an original IP packet inside a new packet and is useful for secured paths between network boundaries.

SNMPv3 adds security capabilities to network management. Its user-based security model can protect against message modification, impersonation and disclosure when appropriate security settings are used.

Encryption makes data unreadable to a party without the required key. It supports confidentiality, but it does not solve every security problem. Key distribution, access control and endpoint protection still matter. These mechanisms also consume processing and require administration. A designer should select and test them against the risks and performance needs of the intended service.
questions.trap: 不要把SNMPv3任意配置都说成必定加密；不死背旧加密算法为现今推荐。
questions.variants: Compare IPsec transport and tunnel modes; discuss encryption overhead.

questions.title: 两种安全与隐私机制
questions.question: Describe two security and privacy mechanisms.
questions.cn: 描述两种安全与隐私机制。
questions.points:
两种机制是加密与身份认证。加密把可读数据变成没有合适密钥就无法理解的形式，帮助保护传输或存储中信息的保密性。例如，加密通信可以降低学生私人信息在传输途中被人读取的风险，密钥也必须受到保护和管理。

身份认证检查用户或设备声称的身份。例如，大学系统可以在允许登录前验证用户凭据，帮助减少未授权访问并支持问责。但认证后还需要适当的授权规则：证明身份不代表能访问每一种资源。

两种机制处理不同需要，可以配合使用。加密不自动提供所有安全目标，身份认证也不阻止所有攻击。选择应依据安全规划中识别的资产、威胁和需求。
questions.answer:
Two mechanisms are encryption and authentication. Encryption changes readable data into a form that cannot be understood without the appropriate key. It helps protect confidentiality when information is transmitted or stored. For example, encrypted communication can reduce the risk of someone reading private student information while it travels across a network. The keys must also be protected and managed.

Authentication checks the identity claimed by a user or device. For example, a university system can check a user's credentials before allowing a login. This helps reduce unauthorized access and supports accountability. However, authentication must be followed by suitable authorization rules: proving an identity does not give access to every resource.

These mechanisms address different needs and can work together. Encryption alone does not automatically provide every security goal, and authentication alone does not prevent every attack. Their selection should follow the assets, threats and requirements identified during security planning.
questions.trap: 只列名称不描述；把authentication和authorization混为一谈；把encryption说成自动满足全部CIA。
questions.variants: 为什么成功登录后，系统仍需要检查用户能访问哪些资料？

questions.title: NAT、firewall、DMZ 与分区
questions.question: Explain how NAT, firewalls and DMZs contribute to network perimeter design.
questions.cn: 说明边界安全与分区。
questions.points: NAT地址转换；firewall访问规则；DMZ隔离外部服务；不是单层万能保护。
questions.answer:
NAT translates addresses between address spaces. It can hide internal addressing from external networks, but address translation alone is not a complete security policy. Authentication, filtering and other protections may still be needed.

A firewall controls communication across a boundary according to rules. A DMZ is a separate zone often used for externally reachable services. It allows access to those services while restricting movement into more sensitive internal networks. Isolation LANs and additional zones can separate groups with different risks or needs.

For example, a public web server can be placed in a DMZ while internal records remain behind another controlled boundary. The design must specify allowed paths and management access. More zones can improve separation but increase cost and operational complexity. Their placement should follow threat analysis and required flows.
questions.trap: NAT不是encryption；DMZ不等于完全可信或无须保护。
questions.variants: Compare perimeter security with internal segmentation; discuss NAT limits.

questions.title: 嵌套安全区与较扁平安全区
questions.question: Compare nested security zones with a less hierarchical security-zone design. How should their placement be justified?
questions.cn: 比较嵌套/较扁平安全区及布置理由。
questions.points: 嵌套：穿越逐层边界；较扁平：按多组功能/敏感性分区，不必每组套在下一组内。由资产、威胁、flow决定；与access/distribution/core是不同视角。
questions.answer:
Nested security zones place protected areas inside larger controlled areas. Traffic reaching a more restricted zone may cross several security boundaries. This can provide layered separation, but it can also create additional processing and management work.

A less hierarchical design places security zones across the network according to particular groups, functions or assets. The zones do not all have to be inside a single chain of increasingly restricted areas. Neither arrangement is automatically best for every network.

Placement should follow threat analysis and required communication. Identify the assets, allowed flows, management paths and effects on performance. For example, externally accessible services can be separated from sensitive internal records without assuming that every internal service needs identical controls. Document the trade-offs and test useful access as well as restrictions. The topology and security-zone views should support each other rather than being treated as the same model.
questions.trap: 扁平分区不等于没有security；多层也不能保证每个跨区flow都满足delay目标。
questions.variants: 先遮住答案复述；再换一个场景说明分类、机制或条件。
questions.kind: 缺口补题；依据课件的AI参考答案

questions.title: 安全架构的 trade-offs
questions.question: Discuss internal and external relationships of security architecture.
questions.cn: 讨论安全机制相互影响及与其他组件的关系。
questions.points: 内部机制依赖/约束；security↔performance、management、addressing。
questions.answer:
Within security architecture, mechanisms can depend on or constrain one another. Encryption requires key management, while address-based rules depend on accurate addressing information. Combining mechanisms therefore needs more than selecting each one separately.

Security also interacts with other component architectures. Inspection and encryption can add processing work and delay. Security rules can block management traffic, even though monitoring and configuration are needed to verify protection. Dynamic addressing and NAT can make address-based access rules and logs harder to interpret.

A designer should compare these effects with the priorities identified during analysis. Selective protection and well-placed zones can protect important assets while controlling unnecessary overhead. Measure the resulting service rather than assuming every security mechanism has the same cost. Document the remaining risks and review the balance when applications or threats change.
questions.trap: 课件15–85%是旧例子，不当普遍性能损失公式。
questions.variants: Explain why maximum inspection everywhere may not be the best overall design.

questions.title: MAC、IP、IPv4 与 IPv6
questions.question: Distinguish MAC and IP addresses and compare IPv4 with IPv6.
questions.cn: 区分地址层次与两个IP版本。
questions.points: MAC链路层；IP逻辑网络层；IPv4 32位、IPv6 128位。
questions.answer:
A MAC address is used for data-link communication, such as delivery of Ethernet frames on a local link. An IP address is a logical network-layer address used to identify an interface and support delivery between networks.

IPv4 addresses contain 32 bits, commonly written as four decimal octets. Each octet contains eight bits. IPv6 addresses contain 128 bits and are commonly written in hexadecimal groups. IPv6 therefore provides a much larger address space.

Addressing must be planned together with routing, location and network structure. The address plan affects aggregation, management and security rules. For example, a computer sending to a remote network normally delivers the local frame to a gateway while the IP packet identifies the final remote destination. Knowing the roles of both addresses helps explain communication across multiple links.
questions.trap: IP通常分配给接口；不要把MAC绝对说成永远不可更改。
questions.variants: Explain why a host needs a gateway for a remote destination.

questions.title: IANA、RIR 与 AS 的分工
questions.question: Explain the roles of IANA, Regional Internet Registries and autonomous systems in the addressing context of this course.
questions.cn: 解释地址和AS号体系中的角色，避免把管理层级当路由协议。
questions.points: IANA顶层协调分配；RIR区域管理（课件以APNIC说明）；AS共同管理/路由策略域，AS number识别。地址分配层级不等于包的转发路径。
questions.answer:
IANA provides top-level coordination for Internet number resources, including the allocation system for IP address blocks and autonomous system numbers.
